top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct invention (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, realised and pushed to the 10^-18 level by Ye's group) that is not just the 2005 comb or 2012 ion-control work. The 10^-18 accuracy has been reproduced independently at several institutes, and the clocks already open new measurements such as gravitational redshift over millimetres and constraints on drifting constants. The Katori and Ye allocation matches the invention and the realisation, and the citation scope is narrow and honest. All eight members support it, so no award is clearly worse.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am an atomic physicist at Lund with no known collaboration with Katori or Ye, though I work in the same broad field of precision laser spectroscopy.
